title: Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which AI-generated video content was used to clone the likeness of a real, named immigration attorney without his consent. The failure did not occur inside a legitimate AI deployment, it occurred at the point of contact between a victim and a scam advertisement distributed through social media. The victim had no way to verify the identity of the person in the video, and the fraudulent material was realistic enough to prompt multiple payments.

The scale reported by the attorney himself, more than 8,000 fake profile videos using his likeness, indicates this was not a single isolated deepfake but a systematic, ongoing operation. The harm arrived in stages, with each additional payment request justified by fabricated document fees, a pattern designed to extend financial extraction after initial trust was established. No platform-level or identity-verification check is reported to have caught or removed the material before the victim was defrauded.

What is not established is who operated the scam, whether any individuals have been charged or prosecuted, and whether the social media platforms hosting the advertisements took any action.

reports.title: Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A Bronx resident who has lived legally in the United States for over a decade fell victim to an artificial intelligence scam while seeking help to become a U.S. citizen. Victor Hernandez responded to a social media advertisement promising citizenship assistance without taking the official exam, and paid $1,500 initially. Scammers then requested additional payments for various documents including his Social Security card and residency card, eventually extracting $4,820 through money transfer apps. Only after his wife expressed suspicion did Hernandez discover the fraudulent scheme.

The fake advertisement used AI technology to impersonate real immigration attorney Angel Leal from Miami, whose identity was cloned without his consent. Leal reports that over 8,000 fake profile videos using his likeness have been created to target immigrants across the country. He emphasizes this represents only a fraction of the actual scams and has made addressing the identity theft a full-time effort. Hernandez, now facing financial hardship including unpaid rent and utilities, reported the crime to law enforcement. Leal recommends hiring attorneys through in-person meetings and warns against anyone requesting payment through cash-sending applications.
